flip.SI-20211101-025343-L: FLIP THRESHOLD: **c2f.** At 7.56 over 300 seconds this is the most quote-dominated book any seat of the round has been entered on; a c2f ceiling anywhere below 7.5 refuses it. c2f is CENSUS-GRADED (CC-M2-21.5: INVERTED, i.e. a negative-sign feature) — the census says high c2f is BAD — and my policy does not read it because a census-graded feature is not a rule. This is the roundest example in the round of the division of labour: I can name the number, the census can sign it, and only the model may use it. Second: T5 passes on 41 contracts via the relative clause (D27) against a 38-contract phase.

novel.SI-20211101-025343-L: novel (day 9): **c2f AS A SEAT-QUALITY NUMBER.** The round's seats now span c2f 0.86 to 7.56 with the extremes at opposite ends of book quality (day 4's TOKYO seat at 0.86 with a $75 spread; today's LONDON seat at 7.56 with a 2-lot bid). CC-M2-21.5 graded c2f an INVERTED feature at era scale on the event cache; if the round's losers concentrate at high c2f, that census is confirmed at the SEAT — the sub-population CC-M2-17.4 says every census must report separately — using seats I did not select on it.

cell_notes: **SIX SEATS, THREE OF THEM IN THE FIRST 76 SECONDS.** The D28 window-collapse hole is not an edge case: on Mondays and after weekends the generator fires OPEN-DYNAMICS at the very top of the session and the core's magnitude terms cannot see anything there.

**THE CARD RULE IS NOW VISIBLY REDIRECTING NKD:** RV1's NKD seats were OPEN-DYNAMICS rows; RV2's are NEWS-WINDOW rows, which is the only NKD class that beats the NKD bulk on both axes of the era card.
